name: Bigbloc Construction Ltd
title: Bigbloc Construction Ltd - 540061 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Volumes up 40% in Q4 but EBITDA margin only 7.36% and FY26 net loss ~INR 9 crore; management says pricing pass-through is lagging raw-material costs up 5-15%, with utilisation at 78% in Q4 and no capex committed.

utilisation.quote: Average capacity utilization during the quarter improved to around 78%.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 35% YoY to INR 87 crore on 40% volume growth, but EBITDA margin was 7.36% and the company posted a net loss of about INR 1 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 sales volume grew 40% YoY to 2,45,870 cubic metres and FY26 volume rose 37% to 8,26,904 cubic metres, with capacity utilisation climbing from 53% in Q1 to 78% in Q4. Revenue from operations was about INR 87 crore (up around 35% YoY) and EBITDA about INR 6 crore (margin 7.36%), but the company still reported a net loss of about INR 1 crore. For FY26, revenue was about INR 283 crore (up around 26%), EBITDA about INR 18 crore (6.21% margin) and net loss about INR 9 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to raw material and fuel cost increases, labour shortages and slow adoption of the new AAC wall panel product, which limited pass-through of cost increases.

financial_highlights.change: around 26% YoY vs INR 225 crore in FY25
FY25 margin about 13% per analyst question

financial_highlights.value: around 78% in Q4; 65% average for FY26 (management also cited 67% for full year)

segments.name: AAC blocks
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margins of about 8% to 10% currently, with a peak of about 25% seen earlier; improvement expected over the next two to three quarters. Western India is the main focus.

segments.name: AAC wall panels
segments.commentary: Management guided gross margins of 50% to 60% and EBITDA margins of 30% to 45%. Full utilisation (80% to 85%) could generate revenue of about INR 100 to 125 crore. Adoption has been slower than expected.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: Management guided gross margins of 40% to 50% and EBITDA margins of 25% to 30%, with about INR 20 to 30 crore revenue from the newly installed plant. Bigbloc Building Ltd's plant at Umargaon began commercial production.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Bigbloc Building Ltd utilisation was about 89%; the Siam Cement Bigbloc Construction Technology JV was about 40%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target of 10% to 20%, with focus on Western India for AAC blocks and construction chemicals and pan-India for AAC panels.
Capacity utilisation expected to rise 10% to 14% in FY27; management targets 75% to 80% utilisation this year, with 80% to 85% as the optimum level.
Management expects to pass on further cost increases over the next two to three quarters, which should improve realisations and margins.
Management expects to return to profit in FY27.
Capacity expansion under consideration: increase at the SIAM JV unit, and land acquired in Madhya Pradesh; expansion plan expected in upcoming quarters.
Peak top-line potential of about INR 350 to 400 crore at current realisations, based on about 1.3 million cubic metres fungible capacity at 80% to 85% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity is about 1.3 million cubic metres per annum across blocks and panels, described as fungible.
Capacity utilisation: Bigbloc Building Ltd about 89%, SIAM Cement Bigbloc JV about 40%.
Expansion options: capacity increase at the SIAM JV for AAC panels and blocks, and a new site in Madhya Pradesh where land has been acquired.
Construction chemicals plant at Umargaon (Bigbloc Building Ltd) has started commercial production.
Rooftop solar installed capacity is 3.3 MW across the company and subsidiaries; about 45% of Q4 power needs came from renewable sources.
demand_pricing: Raw material costs rose about 5% to 15% over the last two to three quarters following the US-Iran conflict, with fuel and LPG price increases also cited.
Margin decline: management attributed about 5% to 6% of the FY26 margin decline to pricing pressure and about 2% to higher operating costs.
Management said Q4 selling prices were broadly similar to Q3, and that some cost increases were passed on from last quarter.
Demand in Q1 FY27 to date is about 15% to 20% above Q1 FY26 and below Q4 FY26 levels; labour shortages slowed volumes in the preceding two to two-and-a-half months.
Channel mix: 55% to 60% via dealers/distributors, 15% to 20% direct builders, about 20% large corporates; no single customer above 3% of sales.

AAC blocks hold about 10% of the volume building-material market versus about 80% for red bricks; management sees 30% to 40% as a longer-term target. Management counts about 150 AAC block manufacturers nationally.
Management said AAC blocks reach about 300 to 350 km from plant due to bulk, and that big builders in the western region and pan-India have shifted to AAC.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY26 margin decline (13% to about 6%) came from pricing versus cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 5% to 6 points came from pricing pressure and about 2 points from higher operating and manufacturing costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook and which regions will drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Target volume growth of 10% to 20%, led by Western India for AAC blocks and chemicals, with AAC panels growing nationally including bullet train station orders and Delhi and Bangalore targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Do you expect realisations to stabilise in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisations fell 5% to 7% over the last year and some cost increases have since been passed on; further pass-through is expected to lift realisations over the next two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How many carbon credits are held and what is the revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: About 150,000 tonnes of carbon credits are held, priced at about $2 to $3; issuance takes about three months before monetisation. No revenue or profit from carbon credits was recognised in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What margins and revenue can the AAC panel and construction chemicals businesses deliver?
qa_highlights.answer: AAC panels are guided to 30% to 45% EBITDA margin and construction chemicals to 25% to 30%; AAC panels could reach INR 100 to 125 crore and chemicals INR 20 to 30 crore at full utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order size and order-book contribution from bullet train station projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders so far are about 40,000 to 50,000 square feet, contributing about 8 to 9 (unit as stated, likely million) to the order book.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on passing through raw material and fuel cost increases, which the company has so far struggled with.
Labour shortages in Western India and the post-Holi and election-period slowdown; watch Q1 FY27 volume growth of 15% to 20%.
AAC panel adoption is slower than expected and is a key driver of the margin improvement the company expects.
Expansion plans (SIAM JV and Madhya Pradesh land) are not yet detailed, and capex sizing and timing were not given.
Monetisation of about 150,000 tonnes of carbon credits and its timing, following an approximately three-month issuance process.
Bullet train order size and contribution to the order book were given only in loose terms, so the order-book visibility remains limited.
Net loss in both Q4 and FY26 persists; the company expects a return to profit in FY27 with no quantified target.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on volume growth and long-term AAC adoption, but cautious and somewhat qualitative on margins and profitability timing. Several answers were hedged with words like "hopefully" and "should be able to", and the company gave no quantified FY27 margin guidance.
key_quotes: Despite a challenging operating environment marked by elevated input costs and labor shortages during the holiday season, we remain focused on driving volume -led growth and expanding our market presence across key regions.
And hopefully in this year, we should be returning to profits again.
So, the drop in margin is mainly because of a little bit of cost pressures coming because of the war scenarios.

adds.what: Construction chemicals plant at Umargaon (Bigbloc Building Ltd), commercial production started, about INR 20-30 crore revenue expected
Capacity increase at SIAM Cement Bigbloc JV unit (AAC panels and blocks), size not quantified
New site in Madhya Pradesh, land acquired, expansion plan expected in upcoming quarters

growth.why: Management targets 10-20% FY27 volume growth and a 10-14% rise in utilisation to 75-80%, with return to profit in FY27; backing is partial, citing ~20% Q1 FY27 volume growth, price pass-through, the Umargaon chemicals plant and unquantified SIAM JV and Madhya Pradesh expansion.
